briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and xAI Grok-4 push AGI timelines forward as compute wars intensify

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this month, driving record funding and regulatory scrutiny. The AGI race has entered a phase of rapid iteration with significant safety gaps persisting. Global compute allocation remains the primary bottleneck.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with improved reasoning while Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus. Google DeepMind's Gemini 3 and Meta's Llama 4.1 both showed gains on agentic benchmarks. xAI Grok-4 and DeepSeek-V3 closed the gap on coding tasks.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and IoT deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped H200 clusters to Microsoft and Oracle while TSMC ramped 2nm production for AI ASICs. New hyperscale data centers broke ground in Texas and UAE.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a coalition including Chinese compute partners?
